assays.assay_description: Pair-housed mice video-recorded for 1 h in their home cage immediately after psilocybin (1.5 mg/kg i.p.) or saline injection, with or without 5-HT2AR (MDL100907) or 5-HT1AR (WAY100635) antagonist pretreatment. Bilateral and unilateral interactions, huddling, allogrooming, mounting and chasing were manually scored (EthoVision XT); huddling analysed as total and in a within-session time course.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (PSI; 1.5 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally in saline.

setup_habituation.evidence: not reported (testing in the animals' own home cage; only 7-day facility acclimation mentioned)

sample_size.evidence: not reported per assay (study-level: Male (n = 182) and female (n = 145))

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin increased huddling in female mice within 60 min post-injection (peaks at 25, 30 and 45 min), with no effect in males. 5-HT1AR and 5-HT2AR antagonism modulated huddling and other social interactions in sex- and receptor-specific ways (both antagonists abolished psilocybin-induced huddling in females).
outcomes.statistics: Females huddling total p = 0.0391; time course 25 min p = 0.0133, 30 min p = 0.0155, 45 min p = 0.0311. Antagonists: 5-HT1AR antagonism reduced huddling in females (saline p = 0.0062; psilocybin p < 0.0001); 5-HT2AR antagonism reduced huddling in PSI females p = 0.0029; males both antagonists reduced huddling in PSI-treated p = 0.0018; 5-HT2AR antagonism reduced unilateral interactions in females (p = 0.0339 saline; p = 0.0328 psilocybin).
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly increased huddling in females within 60 min post-administration (p = 0.0391; Fig. 1D), with peak effects at 25 min (p = 0.0133; Fig. 1E). ... Psilocybin alone did not alter huddling behaviour (Fig. 1G, H) ... in male mice

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: huddling peaked at 25 min (p = 0.0133), 30 min (p = 0.0155) and 45 min (p = 0.0311) post-administration ... H no time-dependent differences in huddling behaviour were observed over 60 min

assays.assay_description: Standard 3-chamber paradigm run in separate cohorts at 4 h, 24 h or 7 d after psilocybin or saline (± MDL100907 or WAY100635). 10 min habituation, then social preference trial (novel mouse vs empty cage) and social novelty trial (second novel mouse vs familiar mouse). Time in chambers, interaction frequency, locomotor activity (binned), grooming, rearing, sociability index and sociability Z-scores quantified.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (PSI; 1.5 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally in saline.

setup_habituation.evidence: Following 10 min habituation, mice explored a novel mouse versus empty cage — habituation is within the test session and locomotor data were recorded during it ('during habituation at 1 min ... and at 5 min'); no separate pre-test apparatus exposure described

setup_restrain.evidence: mice explored a novel mouse versus empty cage (social preference trial)

food_restriction.evidence: standard 3-chamber paradigm; no food in apparatus described

water_restriction.evidence: standard 3-chamber paradigm; no water in apparatus described

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were tested at 4 h, 24 h or 7 d post-injection using the standard 3-chamber paradigm.

sample_size.evidence: not reported per assay (study-level: Male (n = 182) and female (n = 145))

outcomes.summary: At 4 h psilocybin enhanced novelty-seeking and grooming in females with no effect in males (effects attenuated by 5-HT2AR and 5-HT1AR antagonism). At 24 h psilocybin reduced grooming and rearing in males without altering sociability; no effects in females. At 7 d psilocybin reduced the sociability Z-score in females during the social novelty trial (shift toward familiarity) and increased grooming in males.
outcomes.statistics: 4 h females: novel-mouse preference p = 0.0494; grooming p = 0.0443; antagonists attenuated PSI sociability p < 0.03. 24 h: time x sex locomotion F(9.42,197.8) = 2.217, p = 0.0206; male grooming p = 0.0159; male rearing p = 0.0033; 5-HT2AR antagonism reduced Z-score in saline males p = 0.0168, sociability index p = 0.0077. 7 d: time x sex locomotion F(6.096,85.34) = 4.73, p = 0.0003; female sociability Z-score p = 0.0031 (text; p = 0.0023 in Fig. 3 legend); male grooming p = 0.0363 (text; p = 0.0273 in Fig. 3 legend).
outcomes.evidence: At 4 h postadministration, psilocybin enhanced novelty-seeking in female mice (preference for novel mouse, p = 0.0494) and increased grooming (p = 0.0443) ... in male mice, psilocybin ... significantly reduced grooming (p = 0.0159; Fig. 2O) and rearing (p = 0.0033; Fig. 2P). ... At 7 d ... it significantly reduced sociability Z-score only during the social novelty trial (p = 0.0031, Fig. 3H) ... [males] increased grooming behaviour 7 d following treatment (p = 0.0363)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Time in chambers, interaction frequency and locomotor activity were quantified. ... sociability Z-score ... sociability index ... grooming ... rearing

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: significant time x sex interaction in locomotor activity ... with female mice showing significantly higher locomotor activity than males during habituation at 1 min (p = 0.0064) and at 5 min (p = 0.0256)

B4_ethological.evidence: psilocybin ... significantly reduced grooming (p = 0.0159; Fig. 2O) and rearing (p = 0.0033; Fig. 2P)

B5_social.evidence: Two strain-, age- and sex-matched novel mice were used as social stimuli ... mice explored a novel mouse versus empty cage

assays.assay_description: Adapted maternal-motivation paradigm: 10 min habituation to a 60 mm transparent barrier, then exploration of a novel mouse (5 min) and a cage mate (5 min), each confined in a wire cage on the opposite side of the barrier. Latency to first climb/cross, total climbs, latency to sniff, locomotor activity and sociability Z-scores recorded; behavioural data reported 24 h after psilocybin or saline (± MDL100907 or WAY100635). Concurrent NAc GRAB-DA fiber photometry not scored.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (PSI; 1.5 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally in saline.

setup_habituation.evidence: Following 10 min habituation to a 60 mm transparent barrier — within-session phase from which data were reported ('male mice also showed longer latency to cross the barrier than females' during habituation); no separate pre-test exposure described

setup_restrain.evidence: mice explored a novel mouse (5 min) then a cage mate (5 min)

food_restriction.evidence: no food described in the barrier-climbing arena

water_restriction.evidence: no water described in the barrier-climbing arena

time_to_assay.evidence: observed distinct responses in males and females 24 h following administration of saline or psilocybin

sample_size.evidence: not explicitly reported (sex comparison F(1,16) = 5.992 suggests ~18 saline animals)

outcomes.summary: At 24 h, psilocybin increased latency to cross the barrier on arena introduction and increased sociability Z-score toward cage mates in males; females showed a non-significant trend toward increased preference for a novel conspecific. Locomotion was unaffected; antagonists had no significant effects.
outcomes.statistics: Males: latency to cross p = 0.0407; cage-mate sociability Z-score p = 0.0349. Females: novel-mouse sociability trend p = 0.0566; 5-HT2AR antagonism trend p = 0.0694. Baseline sex difference in locomotion F(1,16) = 5.992, p = 0.0263; latency to cross during habituation p = 0.0443.
outcomes.evidence: In male mice, psilocybin had no effect on overall locomotor activity (Fig. 4I) but significantly increased the latency to cross the barrier upon arena introduction (p = 0.0407; Fig. 4J) and enhanced social preference toward cage mates (p = 0.0349; Fig. 4K).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to first climb, total climbs and latency to sniff were recorded; locomotor activity and sociability Z-scores also reported

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: No within-session time-course analysis of behaviour reported for psilocybin effects

B4_ethological.evidence: Latency to first climb, total climbs and latency to sniff were recorded

B5_social.evidence: each confined in a wire cage on the opposite side of the barrier

B6_cognitive.evidence: Assay measures social motivation; no learning/memory requirement described

B7_automated_classification.evidence: No pose-estimation or ML classifier described

E6_spatial.evidence: 60 mm transparent barrier ... each confined in a wire cage on the opposite side of the barrier

E7_social_context.evidence: each confined in a wire cage on the opposite side of the barrier

D2_session_duration.evidence: Following 10 min habituation ... mice explored a novel mouse (5 min) then a cage mate (5 min) — ~20 min session with data reported from the habituation phase

D3_recording_days.evidence: observed distinct responses in males and females 24 h following administration

D5_followup.evidence: 24 h following administration of saline or psilocybin

judge_notes: Retained three behavioural assays (home-cage social behaviour, 3-chamber, barrier climbing); all candidates agreed on this granularity. Antagonist arms and 4 h/24 h/7 d cohorts collapsed into single assays per rubric.
Fiber photometry (NAc GRAB-DA) excluded as neural recording; RFID core body temperature monitoring excluded as physiological (its locomotor data are not reported in results).
Home-cage B1 set to 4-6 (score 2) per modal; gemma's score 3 conflicted with its own value label. E3 bedding scored 0/low since cage contents are not described.

3-chamber and barrier-climbing setup_habituation overridden to not_reported (vs. modal 'yes'): the 10 min habituation is part of the test session and behavioural data were reported from it, so it does not meet the rubric's separate pre-test exposure definition.
3-chamber B2 = Yes (binned locomotion with time x sex interaction, Figs 2B/3B); D2 = 0/low because social trial durations are not stated.

Barrier climbing D2 overridden to 15–60 min (deepseek) because 10 min habituation + 5 + 5 min are explicitly stated and data were collected during habituation; E6 = 1 and B4 = 1 per modal (qwen, deepseek); B6 = 0 per modal.
Strain recorded as C57BL/6J per abstract ('C57BL/6 J'); methods state 'C57Bl/6'.
